items.title: 8.2 Reversible reactions, microscopic events aur dynamic equilibrium (harkat wala equilibrium) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 8.2, printed pages 168-170.

blocks.text: Jab reversible reaction equilibrium par ho to apparently (bazahir) lagta hai ke woh ruk gayi hai (static). Lekin microscopic level par reaction kabhi nahi rukti aur molecules continuously (lagataar) badalte rehte hain. Reactant molecules products mein badalte hain, aur usi waqt reverse process (ulta amal) bhi ho raha hota hai. Is liye hum micro scale par dekhte hain ke kaun se events system ki macroscopic properties par asar dalte hain.

Appropriate conditions (munasib halaat) mein steam (pani ki bhaap) aur carbon monoxide ki reaction lein. In gases ko milane par macroscopic tabdeeliyan nazar aati hain (misal ke taur par concentration badalna). Farz karein dono reactants ke moles barabar le kar reaction shuru ki gayi. Milate hi in ke darmiyan har second sab se zyada collisions (takkar) hoti hain; yeh microscopic events hain. CO aur H₂O ke bonds tootte hain aur naye bonds ban kar H₂ aur CO₂ bante hain. Is liye shuru mein forward reaction ki rate sab se zyada hoti hai. Is se reactants ki concentration kam hoti hai. Jaise jaise H₂O aur CO kharch hote hain, forward reaction slow ho jati hai.

Jab H₂ aur CO₂ ke molecules jama hone lagte hain to reverse reaction bhi shuru ho jati hai. H₂ aur CO₂ ki concentration barhne ke saath in molecules ke darmiyan har second ziada se ziada collisions hoti hain. H₂ aur CO₂ ke bonds tootte hain aur CO aur H₂O ke bonds bante hain.

blocks.alt: Time ke muqable concentration ka graph. Blue curve [CO] ya [H2O] oonchi jagah se shuru ho kar girta hai; magenta curve [CO2] ya [H2] zero se uthta hai aur blue curve ko kaatta hai. Dashed vertical line 'Equilibrium' par dono curves flat (seedhe) ho jate hain, magenta blue se oopar.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.1: Time ke muqable concentration ka plot ([CO] ya [H2O] aur [CO2] ya [H2]) (kitab ki Figure 8.1 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Matlab forward reaction sab se tez rate se shuru ho kar slow hoti jati hai, jabke reverse reaction ki rate shuru mein kam hoti hai, phir barhti hai aur aakhir mein constant ho jati hai.

blocks.alt: Hamara apna graph: time ke muqable rate. Red 'forward rate' oonchi jagah se girta hai, blue 'reverse rate' zero se uthta hai; dashed line par dono barabar ho kar ek seedhi line ban jate hain (rates equal: equilibrium).
blocks.caption: H2O + CO ke liye forward aur reverse rates time ke saath (hamari apni drawing; kitab mein yeh graph nahi).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Pehle graph (Figure 8.1) mein shuru mein sirf CO aur H₂O hain, is liye in ki concentration oonchi hai aur girti hai, jabke H₂ aur CO₂ zero se barhte hain. Dashed line ke baad dono lines flat (seedhi) hain: equilibrium par concentrations nahi badaltin. Doosra graph hamara apna hai aur wajah dikhata hai: forward rate girti hai, reverse rate barhti hai, aur jab dono barabar ho jati hain to equilibrium aa jata hai.

Aakhir kar aisa waqt aata hai jab dono reactions ek hi rate se chalti hain. Is stage par reaction chemical equilibrium mein hoti hai aur reactants aur products ki concentrations constant ho jati hain.
Jab tak system ko kisi tarah disturb (chheda) na jaye, concentrations mein aur koi tabdeeli nahi hoti.

blocks.title: State of chemical equilibrium (chemical equilibrium ki halat)
blocks.text: Reversible reaction ki woh halat jis mein reaction mixture ki composition (banawat) nahi badalti aur forward aur reverse rates barabar hoti hain, chemical equilibrium ki halat kehlati hai.

Figure 8.1 mein ek aam reaction ke liye waqt (time) ke muqable reactants aur products ki concentrations ke graphs hain. Farz karein reactant A badal kar product B banta hai. Graphs dikhate hain ke equilibrium ke baad kya kya ho sakta hai: reactant aur product ki concentrations barabar ho sakti hain (Figure 8.1 a), ya reactant product se kam ya zyada ho sakta hai (Figure 8.1 b aur c). Lekin har graph mein saaf hai ke equilibrium ke baad concentrations constant ho jati hain.

blocks.alt: Teen graphs: time ke muqable reactant A (blue, girta hua) aur product B (magenta, uthta hua) ki concentration. Har graph mein dashed vertical line 'Equilibrium' ke baad dono curves flat hain. (a) A aur B barabar concentration par ruk jate hain. (b) A, B se neeche rukta hai. (c) A, B se oopar rukta hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.1: Time ke muqable concentration ka plot (a) Reactant = Product (b) Reactant < Product (c) Reactant > Product (kitab ki Figure 8.1 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Teenon graphs mein A (blue) girta hai aur B (magenta) barhta hai, aur dashed line ke baad dono flat ho jate hain. Farq sirf aakhri level ka hai: (a) mein A aur B barabar, (b) mein B zyada, (c) mein A zyada. Har case mein equilibrium ka matlab hai concentrations constant, barabar hona zaroori nahi.

Jab concentrations constant ho jayein to lagta hai ke reaction ruk gayi, lekin aisa nahi hai. Microscopic level par bohat activity (harkat) hai. Reactants ke molecules react karte rehte hain, aur products ke molecules bhi aapas mein mil kar wapas reactants bante rehte hain. Forward process ki rate reverse process ki rate ke bilkul barabar hai. Is liye ise dynamic equilibrium (harkat wala equilibrium) kehte hain: molecules lagataar react kar rahe hain, lekin dono rates ek jaisi hain.

items: H₂O + CO mein forward rate shuru mein sab se zyada hoti hai aur reactants kharch hone par girti hai; reverse rate zero se barhti hai.
Dono rates barabar hon to chemical equilibrium: composition constant rehti hai.
Equilibrium dynamic hai: molecules dono taraf react karte rehte hain, chahe aakhri concentrations barabar hon ya na hon.
